title: Syllabus
text:
Note About This Syllabus
Although the core expectations for this class are fixed, the details of readings and assignments may shift based on how the class goes. As a result, there are three important things to keep in mind:

Although details on this syllabus will change, I will not change readings or assignments less than one week before they are due. If I don’t fill in a “To Be Determined” one week before it’s due, it is dropped. If you plan to read more than one week ahead, contact me first.
Closely monitor the class Discord. I will summarize changes in announcements on Discord that should be emailed to everybody in the class if you have notifications turned on.
I will ask the class for voluntary anonymous feedback frequently. Please let me know what is working and what can be improved.

title: Syllabus
text:
Class Sessions
This course follows a discussion- and application-centered format. Most content is encountered through the readings before class, so that our time together can be used to go deeper — not to cover the basics.
Tuesday sessions are discussion-centric. Most of the session will be a conversation about that week’s readings, driven by your questions and ideas. I will use the discussion questions from your 3-2-1 assignments to guide us. This means I expect you to arrive on Tuesdays having done the reading.
Thursday sessions are more like a workshop. We will work through case studies in groups, applying the week’s concepts to real organizational scenarios. Some Thursdays will also be used for project work, peer feedback, or exams.

title: Syllabus
text:
Getting Help
Your first place to look for help should be each other. By asking and answering questions on Discord, you will not only help to build a repository of shared information but also reinforce our learning community.
I will also hold office hours in BRNG 2134 on Tuesdays from 1:00–3:00 PM. Come with specific questions — often just trying to articulate your confusion helps you find the answer.
I will also check Discord at least once a day. I encourage you to post questions there, and to use it as a space where we can help and instruct each other. In general, you should contact me there. I am also available by email. You can reach me at jdfoote@purdue.edu. I try hard to maintain a boundary between work and home and I typically respond only on weekdays during business hours.

title: Syllabus
text:
Participation
I expect you to be an active member of our class. This includes paying attention in class, participating in activities, and being actively engaged in learning, thinking about, and trying to understand the material.
To make sure that everyone has an opportunity to participate and to encourage you to do the assignments, I will randomly select students to discuss readings or to explain portions of homework assignments.

title: Syllabus
text:
Reading Review Assignments
Before most Tuesday sessions, you will complete a short reading review. Its purpose is twofold: to hold you accountable for the reading, and to surface questions that fuel our Tuesday discussion. You have two options — choose whichever works best for you on a given week.

Option A: 3-2-1
Write and submit the following on Brightspace:

3 concepts you learned or connections you made from this week’s reading
2 questions you have or things you don’t fully understand
1 question you think would make a good class discussion question

Post your discussion question to the #discussions channel on Discord as well. Good discussion questions engage with the reading and connect it to other concepts or to the real world. For example:

The reading discussed how organizational culture is created through communication. I think about how different my internship felt from my current job, even in the same industry. What role does management communication play in shaping that difference?
How is organizational power different from personal authority? The reading seemed to conflate them at times.



Option B: AI Conversation
After doing the reading, open an AI tool (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, etc.) and start a conversation with a prompt like this:

“I just read Chapter 4 of my Organizational Communication textbook about Systems and Cultural Approaches. Ask me questions and have a conversation with me to make sure I understand the most important principles and ideas.”

Then have a genuine back-and-forth — answer the AI’s questions, push back if something seems off, ask it to clarify things that are still fuzzy. The goal is to test your own understanding, not to receive a summary. The AI should be doing most of the asking; you should be doing most of the thinking.
Submit two things on Brightspace:

A shareable link to your conversation (both Claude.ai and ChatGPT support this)
A short reflection (a paragraph or two): Discuss what you learned from the conversation and whether you still have questions or confusions after it. What, if anything, would you still like to explore in class?

Conversations where the student is mostly passive — reading AI output rather than engaging with it — won’t receive full credit.

title: Syllabus

Classroom Discussions and Peer Feedback
Throughout the course, you may receive, read, collaborate, and/or comment on classmates’ work. These assignments are for class use only. You may not share them with anybody outside of class without explicit written permission from the document’s author and pertaining to the specific piece.
It is essential to the success of this class that all participants feel comfortable discussing questions, thoughts, ideas, fears, reservations, apprehensions, and confusion. Therefore, you may not create any audio or video recordings during class time nor share verbatim comments with those not in class linked to people’s identities unless you get clear and explicit permission. If you want to share general impressions or specifics of in-class discussions with those not in class, please do so without disclosing personal identities or details.

title: Syllabus
text:
Academic Integrity
While I encourage collaboration, I expect that any work that you submit is your own. Basic guidelines for Purdue students are outlined here, but I expect you to be exemplary members of the academic community. Please get in touch if you have any questions or concerns.

AI Policy
Academic integrity also applies to AI. I am a technology optimist, and an AI optimist. I think AI can be an amazing tool for education and learning, but it can also be misused. The principle I expect you to follow is that you can’t (and shouldn’t) use AI as a shortcut (a tool that gives you answers). Instead, I completely support you using it as a scaffold (a tool that helps you think harder).
Specifically:

Write your own work. Don’t have AI write your reflections, essays, discussion questions, or final project prose. You can use AI to help you brainstorm, or to give you feedback on your writing, but you should be the one doing the writing.
Use AI to understand topics, readings, and concepts. Have AI explain a confusing passage, ask it to define terms, treat it like a patient tutor.
Disclose substantive AI use. I expect you to be transparent about the ways that you use AI in the class.

If you’re unsure whether something crosses a line, ask me. The principle to apply: would this help me learn, or skip learning?

title: Organizational Communication
text:
Welcome to Organizational Communication (COM 324)!
In this class, we will explore how communication shapes and is shaped by organizational life. We will examine the major theories and frameworks for understanding communication within and between organizations, and apply them to real-world contexts.
The top of the page includes links to the syllabus, schedule, and assignments. Check the schedule each week for readings and any assignments due.
